questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Korea makes the most sense I study Korean studies, so not much else makes a lot of sense

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: your experience is only what you make of it

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: the university was very good at sending out email with information so as long as you keep an eye on your email it was fairly okay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: my friend picked me up at the airport, but if you do not know anyone here there are a lot of people to ask and many options, so just ask information at the airport. at the university you can always go to the office of international affairs

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: we got 1 two hour introduction.... in the first week but a lot of mails

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: two dorms next to each other were available, sk global or international house (only women)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
no meal plans, but lots of cafes and student cafeterias on campus, including the global plaza filled with convenience store, restaurants, cafe etc. just in the basement of the dorms. 
I stayed in international house so we had a common kitchen on the 1st floor, though i did not use it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
SK global is the best dormitory as each room has its own bathroom and some 1 man rooms. also open for both male and female, whereas international house is only for female. however the competition to get into sk global is insanely competitive and only the lucky ones get in. 
International house has shared toilet and baths on each floor, so one shares with probably 30 other people, so just take that into account, but the cleaning is done by staff every day beside the weekend.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: just be prepared for what you choose

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: also very competitive, kinda like betting on horses. really need to read up on the rules and criterias for the classes,which you do get mails about. just be aware that some classes might have a quota for exchange students but you can often join anyway by submitting a form of acceptance from the professor in charge of the class to the administration during the last of the 3 rounds. the quota is quite low for graduate classes like only 2 people but just contact the professor and you should be able to get in.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
there are 3 rounds
1) each student get a certain amount of points that they bet on each class, with the highest bitters getting into the class. just check the popularity and the amount of points others have previously bit and make a bet based on that.
2) first come first serve for leftover spots in the classes
3) add and drop in the first week of the semester - here one can submit a form of acceptance (or whatever it is called again) signed by the professor in charged of the class to the administration and still get into a class even though the class might be officially full

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: only received emails and go to office of international affairs

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i got into all of my 3 classes, but only after the 3rd round were I had to get one professor so sign a form to let me into the class and then submit it to administration

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: do a lot of research on the classes, make backup plans for classes, be prepared to contact the professors directly, do not take only classes focused on Korea and Korean culture as the academic level can be lower than other classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i got what I came for but be aware that there are very different teaching methods from KU.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I learned something and the classes were interesting, but that is more due to the classes i chose, which were not any classes i was too familiar with, which made it more fun. 
I did not want to work too hard this semester and learn something outside of Korean studies material i learned at KU, so it fitted me well as I could still do well without having to put in a lot of effort.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Similar amount of reading material to prepare for classes each week, but more explanation of the material than debat of the material like at UCPH. 
a lot of student presentation on the weekly material and more assignments or test during the semester like midterms or porto folio exams. 
more diverse type of examinationations at Yonsei than at UCPH but also did not feel quite as academic as what is demanded at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International relations (introduction course)
Inter-Korean relations
Understanding Korean society through popular music

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Inter-Korean relations
because it felt useful and very currently relatable and important. the professor was great and had great knowledge and insight. no midterm exam and very comprehendable and doable final exam.

school clubs and club parties

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
mobilephone and the price of having fun as much as i did :)
school club

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
i joined the bowling club and was very happy with that, but quite expensive. also remember many clubs allow exchange students but many require a certain level of korean language skills
i also joined all the exchange student clubs i could and attended the parties there so set money aside for that.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
many events like amusement park, kimchi making, MT through the exchange student clubs like Yonsei global and attending yonko games and all the cheer events leading up to the games. 
no festival in the fall.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: try joining a school club and definitely go to the yonko games (sports games against Korea university and yonsei university) and all the cheer events leading up to the games. the most fun ever and something danish universities just do not do.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go anywhere than stay on campus as one easily just stays on campus doing the weekdays as its cheap and close by and the classes may end late.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: not a big problem for me personally as i have been to korea a few times and speak the language okay well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
be proactive in introducing yourselves and keep up the contact via instagram or so. 
learn some korean

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none personally

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the helpsomeness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
choose your classes carefully depending on what your goal is (academically or cultural experience and fun) 
you just need to pass the classes so enjoy korea as much as possible
always prepare for extra costs

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: 4 year students or senior  (aka last year of study) are allowed to take 1 master course so try and do that

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting away from KU system for a bit and being able to have so much diverse fun in seoul

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: getting the money to last

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.answer: Yes
